statement: Relative employment index of ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupation quintile falls >= 5 pts from its 2026 level (Stanford Digital Economy Lab 'Canaries' series; last 2027 release)
status_at_phase_end: Series did not exist in 2023 (the Canaries index was first published in 2025). In-phase, the occupational AI-exposure measures that later underpin such quintiles were first published (Mar 2023), but no age-by-exposure employment index was available.

items.summary: No age-by-AI-exposure employment index existed during 2023; the indicator's source series begins later.
items.detail: Stanford Digital Economy Lab 'Canaries in the Coal Mine' series first released in 2025 (outside phase). Data-gap recorded as of phase end. Context source below is the in-phase exposure measure.

items.summary: A working paper by a frontier developer's researchers and academics published occupation-level exposure scores to large language models, an early look at labour-market impact potential (exposure, not observed employment change).
items.detail: Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, Rock, 'GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models', arXiv:2303.10130, v1 2023-03-17, v5 2023-08-21 (verified via web_extract this run; abstract text not captured, so only title/dates relied on).
